The What Matters Most Meeting Checklist

What to ask, write down and leave open before the family decides.

Download PDF

There's a care decision to make for your loved one, and the family is getting together to talk about it. Before anyone compares options, see that these have been asked and written down. Check what you've done. Anything unchecked is a conversation still to have, not a verdict on your family.

Ask

Write down

Leave open

What this checklist doesn't do

It helps you ask and write down. It doesn't say who is right, what a checked or unchecked box means, or what the family should choose. That takes your loved one, the whole family, and the next step below.

Ready for the next step?

You've asked, and you've written down what was said. The care interview adds the other half: it walks you through your loved one's situation area by area, so what matters to them sits beside a full picture of what the decision is about, and turns your answers into a Family Care Profile you can bring to any care conversation.

Create Your Free Family Care Profile ›

Where this comes from

The item marked 1 follows the National Institute on Aging's advice to ask the person directly. The item marked 2 follows the Family Caregiver Alliance's point that a family meeting should give everyone a chance to be heard. The rest come from the Family Care Roadmap's own working list for this step.

  1. National Institute on Aging, Does an Older Adult in Your Life Need Help?
  2. Family Caregiver Alliance, Holding a Family Meeting
